We need to find template that reproduces Still-Gennari reaction retrosynthesis for target molecule C#CC(=O)OCC (propargyl ester? Actually structure: propargyl acetate? Wait: C#C C(=O)OCC is propargyl acetate? Actually C#C- C(=O)O-CC (ethyl propargyl acetate). Reaction: Still-Gennari HWE forms Z-alkene from aldehyde + phosphonate ester. Our target is alkyne ester, not alkene. But description says triple bond changed to single bond, forming alkene and ester. So retrosynthesis: break C=C double bond and ester formed. So precursor would be aldehyde (R-CHO) and phosphonate ester (with electron-withdrawing groups). The target SMILES: C#CC(=O)OCC. Wait that has alkyne attached to carbonyl (propargyl acetate). The reaction would convert alkyne to alkene? Actually Still-Gennari forms alkene from aldehyde + phosphonate, not from alkyne. Maybe the target is product of Still-Gennari: an alkene with ester group. But our SMILES shows alkyne, not alkene. Maybe they consider triple bond changed to single bond (i.e., alkyne to alkene). So product is alkene, but SMILES shows alkyne. Could be they gave starting material? Hmm.

We need to find template that when applied to molecule reproduces reaction (i.e., retrosynthetic step). So we need a template that breaks C=C double bond and forms alkyne? Actually retrosynthesis: from product (alkene) to aldehyde + phosphonate. But our molecule is alkyne ester, maybe product after reaction? Not sure.

Look for template with functional groups: C-C double bonds formed, carboxylic esters formed, alkyne broken. The search earlier gave many templates but not specific. The first result (reaction_id 959896) seems unrelated large molecule.

So likely reaction_id.
